title: Universal Drag Handles and Drop Zone Highlighting
description: Add a consistent drag-handle affordance (grip-vertical icon) to every draggable UI element in ui/js/react/index.tsx, and highlight all valid drop zones (passively) while a compatible drag is in flight, keeping the existing stronger indicator on the currently hovered target. Handle-only drag initiation on select-first elements (panel tabs, mode/window tabs, reorderable tree rows); whole-surface drag retained on drag-first elements (tree-unit headers, catalogue/palette items, mode tab-gap stack drag, DraggableAvatar). Handles always visible (muted, brighten on hover). Plan approved at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/ui-everything-that-is-silly-wolf.md.
summary:
Found and fixed the actual root cause of the hover regression in ui/js/react/index.tsx (the prior round's :has()-removal fix addressed a real but secondary issue — it wasn't the reason hover was completely missing).

Root cause: `selfHoverExcludingHandle`/`groupHoverExcludingHandle` were FUNCTIONS that built Tailwind class strings via runtime template-literal interpolation (`` `hover:not-data-[handle-hovered=true]:${utility}` ``). Tailwind's build only discovers utility classes by statically scanning source file TEXT for literal class-name-shaped substrings — it never executes JavaScript. Since the fully-assembled compound class string (e.g. `hover:not-data-[handle-hovered=true]:bg-hover-interactive-fill`) never appeared as literal text anywhere in the source — only the template skeleton and the separate bare utility-name argument existed — the scanner never found it and Tailwind silently generated zero CSS for every one of these classes. This means hover was completely non-functional for every element using them (`interactiveActiveFillClass`, `panelTabButtonClass`, `modeDockTabClassName`, both tree row chrome functions) — matching exactly what was reported ("no hover effect outside the drag handle" — actually no hover effect at all, since the base `hover:` utility was ALSO only ever expressed through these broken functions).

This is why the prior round's manual CLI verification (feeding literal candidate strings directly to `compile().build(candidates)`) gave false confidence: it tested "if Tailwind knew about this candidate, does it compile correctly" but never tested "does Tailwind's real scanner ever discover this candidate from the actual source text" — which is the step that was actually broken.

Fix: replaced both functions with a fixed set of fully-literal string constants (`hoverExcludingHandleBgFillClass`, `hoverExcludingHandleTextEmphasizedClass`, `hoverExcludingHandleActiveBgClass`, `hoverExcludingHandleActiveBorderClass`, `groupHoverExcludingHandleBgFillClass`), each written out completely so the literal text exists verbatim in the source. Updated all 5 call sites (`interactiveActiveFillClass` ×3, `panelTabButtonClass` ×2, `modeDockTabClassName` ×2, `treeRowChromeShellClasses` ×1, `treeRowChromeContentFillClasses` ×1) to reference these constants instead of calling the removed functions.

Verification (this time genuinely end-to-end, not just build-time-correctness-if-discovered): used `@tailwindcss/oxide`'s `Scanner.scanFiles()` directly against the real `index.tsx` file content to confirm the native scanner now finds all 5 target candidate strings (previously would have found none, since they only existed as un-assembled fragments) — then piped those scanner-discovered candidates through `@tailwindcss/node`'s `compile()` against the project's real theme file and confirmed all 5 rules generate with correct selectors and correct color values, no `:has()` anywhere. Also re-ran typecheck (75 pre-existing unrelated errors, unchanged), lint (same single pre-existing rule-definition error), the `check-no-raw-colors` guardrail (zero violations), and tests (257 passed / 14 pre-existing unrelated failures, identical set) — all show no regressions.

Given two rounds of this exact class of bug (a plausible-looking CSS/Tailwind fix that turned out broken in ways static verification alone didn't catch until traced to the actual build pipeline), a live browser check of hover behavior on panel tabs, mode tabs, and tree rows is strongly recommended before considering this fully resolved.
